question.worked_solution:
First, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}x}{(x+1)\sqrt{9-(3x+3)^{2}}} & =\int \frac{\text{d}x}{(x+1)\sqrt{9-9{(x+1)}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}}\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=x+1.$ Then, we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arsech}⁡(x+1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
